# PUBG on Waydroid: DNS investigation

> A real-world, evidence-documented troubleshooting case involving PUBG Mobile running in Waydroid on Linux. A missing local hostname mapping correlated with DNS SERVFAIL and launch/transition lag; adding one host mapping made the tested resolvers answer successfully, after which the user reported that launch and transition lag disappeared.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/shooher95/pubg-waydroid-dns-investigation/blob/main/README.md): overview, tested environment, workaround, verification, rollback.
- [Evidence and timeline](https://github.com/shooher95/pubg-waydroid-dns-investigation/blob/main/docs/evidence.md): observed facts, user-reported results, hypotheses, and open questions.
- [DNS capture and dnsmasq trace](https://github.com/shooher95/pubg-waydroid-dns-investigation/blob/main/docs/dns-resolution-capture.md): sanitized packet-capture and syscall-trace findings.
- [Translation diagnostics](https://github.com/shooher95/pubg-waydroid-dns-investigation/blob/main/docs/translation-diagnostics.md): separate NDK translation / Houdini investigation; not established as the DNS cause.
- [Verification script](https://github.com/shooher95/pubg-waydroid-dns-investigation/blob/main/scripts/verify-dns-fix.sh): read-only check of the hostname mapping and resolution.

## Core finding

Before the workaround, the Waydroid client (192.168.240.112) queried the host-side resolver (192.168.240.1) for the single-label name `waydroid.`. dnsmasq forwarded the request to systemd-resolved at 127.0.0.53, which returned SERVFAIL in the captured trace. The host's `/etc/hosts` had no matching entry.

The operator added:

```text
192.168.240.1 waydroid
```

After flushing the resolver cache, both tested resolver endpoints returned 192.168.240.1 for `waydroid.`. The user then reported that PUBG launched and the previously observed launch / button-triggered transition lag disappeared.

## Important limitations

- This is one machine's observed result, not a universal fix or performance guarantee.
- The evidence does not identify which Android process requested `waydroid.`.
- It does not prove that the DNS issue caused every PUBG freeze or any remaining map / match / reconnect stall.
- Verify that 192.168.240.1 is still the host-side Waydroid gateway before applying the mapping elsewhere.
- Raw packet captures and traces are intentionally not included; only sanitized findings are published.
